user.title: Add a CrowdSec instance
user.description:
Home Assistant reads the Prometheus metrics endpoint and the Local API (LAPI) of the instance. Machine credentials are the ones registered with `cscli machines add`.

{error_detail}

data_description.bouncer_api_key: Only needed for an exact decision count; otherwise the cs_active_decisions metric is used.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure CrowdSec
reconfigure.description:
Change the addresses or the credentials of this instance. Leave the password and the bouncer key empty to keep the stored ones.

{error_detail}

data.bouncer_api_key: Bouncer API key (leave empty to keep)

data_description.bouncer_api_key: Add one here if the ban table stays empty — some CrowdSec versions only serve the decision list to bouncers.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate CrowdSec
reauth_confirm.description:
The LAPI rejected the stored credentials.

{error_detail}

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the instance. Check URLs, port and tunnel.
error.invalid_auth: The LAPI rejected the machine credentials. Check machine ID and password, and whether the machine is validated (cscli machines list).
error.invalid_auth_metrics: The metrics endpoint denied access. It is usually unauthenticated — a proxy or tunnel in front of it is likely asking for credentials.
error.invalid_auth_alerts: The login succeeded, but the LAPI denies the alert query. See details below — only the 24h alert sensors are affected.
error.invalid_auth_bouncer: The bouncer API key was rejected. Leave the field empty to use the cs_active_decisions metric instead.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: These credentials belong to a different CrowdSec instance.

data.bouncer_idle_intervals: Intervals without bouncer queries before a problem
data.no_lines_intervals: Intervals without log lines before a problem

data_description.timeout: Must be lower than the polling interval. Raise it if the instance is reached over VPN or a slow proxy.
data_description.no_lines_intervals: How many cycles in a row CrowdSec may process no log lines before Status reports it as blind. A quiet instance needs a few; at the default polling interval one cycle is one minute.
data_description.alerts_limit: Size of a single alert query. If it is hit, the time window is split and queried again, so the 24h numbers stay complete. Very high values slow down every cycle.
data_description.alerts_full_interval: How often the whole 24h window is refetched. In between, every cycle only asks for the minutes since the last one, so a new ban is still noticed immediately — this only controls how much load the instance sees.

error.timeout_too_long: The timeout must be lower than the polling interval, otherwise polling cycles overlap.
error.full_interval_too_short: The full alert refresh must not be shorter than the polling interval — every cycle would be a full query.

decisions_unavailable.title: CrowdSec is not handing over the ban list

confirm.title: Add a bouncer API key
confirm.description:
The instance "{name}" refuses the decision list to the machine token — some CrowdSec versions only serve it to bouncers. Create a key with `cscli bouncers add homeassistant` and paste it here; the ban table then fills up again.

{error_detail}

abort.entry_not_found: This CrowdSec instance no longer exists.

alerts_truncated.title: CrowdSec 24h numbers are incomplete
alerts_truncated.description: The instance "{name}" reports more alerts in one minute than a single query returns ({limit}). Splitting the time window did not help, so "Alerts 24h", "New bans 24h" and the top lists are truncated. Raise "Alerts per query" in the integration options.

entry_not_loaded.message: The CrowdSec instance "{name}" is not loaded.

invalid_duration.message: "{duration}" is not a usable ban duration: {error}

invalid_ip.message: "{ip}" is not a valid IP address or range.

ban_ip.name: Ban IP
ban_ip.description: Creates a ban decision for an IP address or range.

config_entry_id.name: Instance
config_entry_id.description: The CrowdSec instance the decision is added to.

ip.name: IP address
ip.description: Single address or CIDR range, e.g. 192.0.2.10 or 192.0.2.0/24.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the ban lasts, e.g. 30m, 4h or 1h30m. CrowdSec has no day unit — use 168h instead of 7d.

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: Shown as the scenario in cscli decisions list.

unban_ip.name: Unban IP
unban_ip.description: Removes all decisions for an IP address or range.

config_entry_id.name: Instance
config_entry_id.description: The CrowdSec instance the decisions are removed from.

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Fetches metrics and alerts immediately instead of waiting for the next interval.
